title: Job, Chapter 18 (Leningrad Codex)
source: Leningrad Codex folios (Internet Archive, WSRP photographs) + tanach.us LC folio index + UXLC Hebrew + KJV
description: Job 18 on folio 402r of the Leningrad Codex (1008 AD), the oldest complete Hebrew Bible. Hebrew from the UXLC transcription of this manuscript; English KJV.
introduction:
Job chapter 18 from the Leningrad Codex (Codex Leningradensis, National Library of Russia, Firkovich EBP. I B 19a), copied in Cairo by Samuel ben Jacob and dated 1008/1009 AD, the oldest complete manuscript of the Hebrew Bible and the base text of the Biblia Hebraica editions. This chapter stands on folio 402r.

This entry meets the strict three-criteria standard of the Theosis Library:

  1. Manuscript scan: the specific folio side(s) carrying each section's verses, from the full-colour West Semitic Research Project photographs of the codex as redistributed on Internet Archive (item Leningrad_Codex_Color_Images, marked Creative Commons Public Domain Mark 1.0). Folio-to-verse ranges come from the tanach.us LC folio index, which was derived from the West Semitic Research Project's published index; each section links only to the page(s) whose recorded verse range contains its verses.
  2. Original text: the verbatim Hebrew of this manuscript in the Unicode/XML Leningrad Codex (UXLC 2.5 build 27.6, tanach.us), a transcription of Firkovich B 19a with vowels and cantillation, released without restriction on the biblical text.
  3. English translation: the King James Version (1611, public domain), retrieved verbatim from bolls.life (KJV text, Strong's numbers stripped).
translator_notes: פ and ס mark the open and closed paragraph breaks visible as gaps in the manuscript columns.

translation.original_text: <sup>1</sup>וַ֭יַּעַן בִּלְדַּ֥ד הַשֻּׁחִ֗י וַיֹּאמַֽר׃ <sup>2</sup>עַד־אָ֤נָה ׀ תְּשִׂימ֣וּן קִנְצֵ֣י לְמִלִּ֑ין תָּ֝בִ֗ינוּ וְאַחַ֥ר נְדַבֵּֽר׃ <sup>3</sup>מַ֭דּוּעַ נֶחְשַׁ֣בְנוּ כַבְּהֵמָ֑ה נִ֝טְמִ֗ינוּ בְּעֵינֵיכֶֽם׃ <sup>4</sup>טֹֽרֵ֥ף נַפְשׁ֗וֹ בְּאַ֫פּ֥וֹ הֲ֭לְמַּעַנְךָ תֵּעָ֣זַב אָ֑רֶץ וְיֶעְתַּק־צ֝֗וּר מִמְּקֹמֽוֹ׃ <sup>5</sup>גַּ֤ם א֣וֹר רְשָׁעִ֣ים יִדְעָ֑ךְ וְלֹֽא־יִ֝גַּ֗הּ שְׁבִ֣יב אִשּֽׁוֹ׃ <sup>6</sup>א֖וֹר חָשַׁ֣ךְ בְּאָהֳל֑וֹ וְ֝נֵר֗וֹ עָלָ֥יו יִדְעָֽךְ׃ <sup>7</sup>יֵֽ֭צְרוּ צַעֲדֵ֣י אוֹנ֑וֹ וְֽתַשְׁלִיכֵ֥הוּ עֲצָתֽוֹ׃ <sup>8</sup>כִּֽי־שֻׁלַּ֣ח בְּרֶ֣שֶׁת בְּרַגְלָ֑יו וְעַל־שְׂ֝בָכָ֗ה יִתְהַלָּֽךְ׃
translation.text: <sup>1</sup>Then answered Bildad the Shuhite, and said, <sup>2</sup>How long will it be ere ye make an end of words? mark, and afterwards we will speak. <sup>3</sup>Wherefore are we counted as beasts, and reputed vile in your sight? <sup>4</sup>He teareth himself in his anger: shall the earth be forsaken for thee? and shall the rock be removed out of his place? <sup>5</sup>Yea, the light of the wicked shall be put out, and the spark of his fire shall not shine. <sup>6</sup>The light shall be dark in his tabernacle, and his candle shall be put out with him. <sup>7</sup>The steps of his strength shall be straitened, and his own counsel shall cast him down. <sup>8</sup>For he is cast into a net by his own feet, and he walketh upon a snare.

translation.original_text: <sup>9</sup>יֹאחֵ֣ז בְּעָּקֵ֣ב פָּ֑ח יַחֲזֵ֖ק עָלָ֣יו צַמִּֽים׃ <sup>10</sup>טָמ֣וּן בָּאָ֣רֶץ חַבְל֑וֹ וּ֝מַלְכֻּדְתּ֗וֹ עֲלֵ֣י נָתִֽיב׃ <sup>11</sup>סָ֭בִיב בִּֽעֲתֻ֣הוּ בַלָּה֑וֹת וֶהֱפִיצֻ֥הוּ לְרַגְלָֽיו׃ <sup>12</sup>יְהִי־רָעֵ֥ב אֹנ֑וֹ וְ֝אֵ֗יד נָכ֥וֹן לְצַלְעֽוֹ׃ <sup>13</sup>יֹ֭אכַל בַּדֵּ֣י עוֹר֑וֹ יֹאכַ֥ל בַּ֝דָּ֗יו בְּכ֣וֹר מָֽוֶת׃ <sup>14</sup>יִנָּתֵ֣ק מֵ֭אָהֳלוֹ מִבְטַח֑וֹ וְ֝תַצְעִדֵ֗הוּ לְמֶ֣לֶךְ בַּלָּהֽוֹת׃ <sup>15</sup>תִּשְׁכּ֣וֹן בְּ֭אָהֳלוֹ מִבְּלִי־ל֑וֹ יְזֹרֶ֖ה עַל־נָוֵ֣הוּ גָפְרִֽית׃ <sup>16</sup>מִ֭תַּחַת שָֽׁרָשָׁ֣יו יִבָ֑שׁוּ וּ֝מִמַּ֗עַל יִמַּ֥ל קְצִירֽוֹ׃
translation.text: <sup>9</sup>The gin shall take him by the heel, and the robber shall prevail against him. <sup>10</sup>The snare is laid for him in the ground, and a trap for him in the way. <sup>11</sup>Terrors shall make him afraid on every side, and shall drive him to his feet. <sup>12</sup>His strength shall be hungerbitten, and destruction shall be ready at his side. <sup>13</sup>It shall devour the strength of his skin: even the firstborn of death shall devour his strength. <sup>14</sup>His confidence shall be rooted out of his tabernacle, and it shall bring him to the king of terrors. <sup>15</sup>It shall dwell in his tabernacle, because it is none of his: brimstone shall be scattered upon his habitation. <sup>16</sup>His roots shall be dried up beneath, and above shall his branch be cut off.

translation.original_text: <sup>17</sup>זִֽכְרוֹ־אָ֭בַד מִנִּי־אָ֑רֶץ וְלֹא־שֵׁ֥ם ל֝֗וֹ עַל־פְּנֵי־חֽוּץ׃ <sup>18</sup>יֶ֭הְדְּפֻהוּ מֵא֣וֹר אֶל־חֹ֑שֶׁךְ וּֽמִתֵּבֵ֥ל יְנִדֻּֽהוּ׃ <sup>19</sup>לֹ֘א נִ֤ין ל֣וֹ וְלֹא־נֶ֣כֶד בְּעַמּ֑וֹ וְאֵ֥ין שָׂ֝רִ֗יד בִּמְגוּרָֽיו׃ <sup>20</sup>עַל־י֭וֹמוֹ נָשַׁ֣מּוּ אַחֲרֹנִ֑ים וְ֝קַדְמֹנִ֗ים אָ֣חֲזוּ שָֽׂעַר׃ <sup>21</sup>אַךְ־אֵ֭לֶּה מִשְׁכְּנ֣וֹת עַוָּ֑ל וְ֝זֶ֗ה מְק֣וֹם לֹא־יָדַֽע־אֵֽל׃ ס
translation.text: <sup>17</sup>His remembrance shall perish from the earth, and he shall have no name in the street. <sup>18</sup>He shall be driven from light into darkness, and chased out of the world. <sup>19</sup>He shall neither have son nor nephew among his people, nor any remaining in his dwellings. <sup>20</sup>They that come after him shall be astonied at his day, as they that went before were affrighted. <sup>21</sup>Surely such are the dwellings of the wicked, and this is the place of him that knoweth not God.
